To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BRL 391223 is a new antiviral agent which is highly active against herpes simplex virus type I and type 2 in vitro, but less so against varicella-zoseter virus and cytomegalovirus.

BRL 391223, a new guanosine derivative, was highly potent and selective for HSV-1 and HSV-2 and was more effective than ACY in reducing virus yield and was more effective in persistently inhibiting viral replication.

BRL 391223 is a potent antiherpesvirus compound which is more active than ACY in plaque reduction tests and in virus yield reduction tests in MRC- 5 cells and that it has a long-lasting effect on virus replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of 9-(2-hydroxy-ethoxymethyl)-guanine (HEM-G) and its derivatives, and the evaluation of their anti-herpesvirus activities in cell culture.
the synthesis of new compounds with antiviral activity.
the development of a new antiviral agent with broad spectrum activity against the herpesviruses.

BRL 391123 is more active than ACY in cell culture against HSV-1, HSV-2, and varicella zoster virus.
BRL 391123 is a more effective antiherpesvirus agent than ACV in cell culture.
BRL 391123 is a promising antiherpesvirus compound which is active against HSV, varicella-zooster virus, and several animal alphaherpesviruses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRL 39122 is a more active antiherpesvirus agent than ACV, and it is likely that this is due to its more efficient inhibition of virus replication in cells.
BRL 39122 was a more potent and more active antiherpesvirus agent than ACV, but that its spectrum of activity was narrower than that of ACV.

the BRL 39122 is an effective antiviral drug that is more active than ACY.
